note: The narrators' and authors' own words: 'Jesus, who is called Christ' (Matt 1:16); 'the gospel of Jesus Christ' (Mark 1:1, as Mark titles his book); 'He admonished the disciples not to tell anyone that He was the Christ' (Matt 16:20); the demons 'knew He was the Christ' (Luke 4:41); 'these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ' (John 20:31); what the apostles (Acts 5:42), Saul (9:22), Paul (18:5) and Apollos (18:28) proclaimed, 'that Jesus is the Christ'; 'everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ' (1 John 5:1; 2:22).

Peter's words: 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God' (Matt 16:16); 'You are the Christ' (Mark 8:29); 'The Christ of God' (Luke 9:20); and preaching, 'God has made this Jesus, whom you crucified, both Lord and Christ!' (Acts 2:36), 'Jesus, the Christ, who has been appointed for you' (Acts 3:20).
Andrew says to his brother Simon, 'We have found the Messiah'; John adds, 'which is translated as Christ' (John 1:41).
Martha's words: 'Yes, Lord, I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, who was to come into the world' (John 11:27).
The angel's words to the shepherds: 'Today in the city of David a Savior has been born to you. He is Christ the Lord!' (Luke 2:11).
Paul's words at Thessalonica: 'This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ' (Acts 17:3).
Mark: asked by the high priest, 'Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?' (14:61), Jesus answers 'I am' (14:62).

John, as John gives it: the Samaritan woman says, 'I know that Messiah' (John adds, 'called Christ') 'is coming' (4:25); Jesus answers, 'I who speak to you am He' (4:26) -- the 'He' is the Messiah she has just named.

Matthew, as Matthew gives it: charged under oath, 'Tell us if You are the Christ, the Son of God' (26:63), Jesus answers 'You have said it yourself. But I say to all of you, from now on you will see the Son of Man ...' (26:64).
